about.title: Simi Valley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Simi Valley is a city of about 126,788 people, and most of its daily driving funnels through a handful of routes. In 2025, the city logged 357 injury collisions, 500 people hurt, and 5 traffic deaths, according to public records. The corridors carrying the largest share of those reports were SR-118, the Ronald Reagan Freeway, along with Los Angeles Avenue, Cochran Street, and Royal Avenue. Reports cluster on Wednesdays between 5 and 7 p.m., when the evening commute is at its heaviest. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the days that follow matter. Photos, witness names, medical visits, and the police report number all become part of your claim. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who handles car accident cases in Ventura County. Under California law, you generally have two years to file, and fault can be shared without erasing your right to compensation. Tell us what happened, and we will make the introduction.

items.title: Deadlines Are Tracked From Day One
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident claims, but that window can shrink to six months if a city, county, or state agency is involved. The attorney you are matched with will identify which deadline applies before it becomes a problem.

items.title: Shared Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible, you can still recover the portion attributable to the other driver. There is also no statutory cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in an ordinary car crash case.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, and You Keep Control
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they are paid only if there is a recovery. Our service is free, and you are never obligated to hire anyone we introduce.

items.question: My crash happened on the 118 freeway in Simi Valley. Who investigated, and how do I get the report?
items.answer: Collisions on SR-118 are typically handled by the California Highway Patrol rather than the Simi Valley Police Department, so the report request goes to the CHP area office that responded. Crashes on surface streets like Cochran or Royal Avenue are usually documented by Simi Valley police. An attorney can request the correct report and check it for errors that might affect your claim.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling for a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise not to until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use casual remarks about how you feel or what you remember to reduce what they pay. Instead, focus on preserving evidence: keep photos, save medical records, and write down your own account while it is fresh.

items.question: I did not feel hurt at the scene, but my neck and back started aching two days later. Is it too late?
items.answer: Delayed symptoms are common after rear-end and side-impact crashes, and they do not disqualify you from a claim. See a doctor as soon as the pain appears so there is a medical record connecting it to the collision. California's two-year filing deadline gives you time, though acting early helps protect evidence and witness memories.
